_comment: The claims the verify skill must handle correctly, planted in the fixture.
The corpus vouches for provenance, not truth — so a vetted story file carrying
a publicly wrong claim is a legal corpus state, and it is exactly the state
`verify` exists to catch. The trap: the Bellhaven reporting story (2016)
describes its transform as using PostgreSQL generated columns, a feature that
shipped in PostgreSQL 12, in 2019. The control: the same file's
anachronisms_corrected: block already settles 'data mesh', and settled entries
`planted` patterns must stay in the target file (offline mode asserts this —
a trap quietly deleted must not leave the live assertions passing over
nothing). `expect_in_report` patterns must appear in a live run's report.
`documented_in` tethers each case to the section that explains it.

cases.rule: verify `[CITE-OR-ASK]` — the finding fires, and carries a citation; interview `[CHECK-THE-CLAIM]` is the rule it enforces
cases.why: Generated columns shipped in PostgreSQL 12 (2019); the story's work is 2016. One search by an interviewer kills the sentence.

cases.rule: verify — `anachronisms_corrected:` is the settled ledger; settled entries are not reopened
cases.why: 'data mesh' is already corrected and logged in the fixture. The entry must stay planted so a live run has a settled correction to leave alone.
